notes.30.16: ꜥꜣt is a costly stone (restored and doubtful); mḥy (doubtful) and sqd are not understood, perhaps terms for setting or inlay; 'purified with gold' (swꜥb m nbw) may mean mounted in gold.
notes.39.12: 39.15: ꜥḏ is uncertain ('cut up'?), and the syntax of the line is loose. 39.16: nzpw is not understood; 'he' may be Ra or Apophis; bꜣgj 'weary, slack'.
notes.39.31: 39.32-39.34 are obscure. bnn is taken as 'potency, begetting', zbn as 'slip away'. In 39.34 ꜣ may be an interjection or particle; a negative ('you shall never copulate') may be meant.

nodes.text: Words to be spoken over a scarab of *ꜥꜣ[t]*-stone(?), *mḥy*(?), *sqd*, purified with gold, placed inside the heart of a man for whom the Opening of the Mouth has been performed, anointed with the finest *nwd*-unguent.
To be said over it as magic.
Your injury is decreed by Maat;
those who are on the road overthrow you.
Fall, slither away, Apophis, enemy of Ra!
O, depart, cut-up one(?), in the east of the sky, at the sound of the storm-cloud roaring, when the gates of the horizon open before Ra!
He goes forth weary, then, from the *nzpw*.
what she has done against you.
You are sick on her account, a portion for ever(?).
You have let your potency(?) slip away for ever;
ah, you copulate for ever(?), enemy of Ra!
He drives back your face, you whom Ra hates.
As for one who knows this book on earth, or [if] it is put in writing on his coffin, he will go forth by day in any form he wishes, and enter his mansion, and he will not be turned back.
